cli.input: --input selects the inventory positions file only; default /app/data/inventory_positions.json

description: Output contract for the requirements planner. Shapes, paths, field lists and sort orders only; no derivation rule lives here.

exception_queue.serialisation: one compact JSON object per line, trailing newline
exception_queue.sort: ascending by release_day, then item_id, then receipt_day, then kind, then qty; the key covers every field a row carries, so no two rows can tie on it without being identical

item_plan.serialisation: JSON array, two-space indent, trailing newline
item_plan.sort: ascending by item_id; planned_orders ascending by receipt_day

summary.serialisation: JSON object, two-space indent, trailing newline

inventory_positions.serialisation: JSON array, two-space indent, trailing newline
inventory_positions.sort: ascending by item_id; scheduled_receipts ascending by receipt_id, and where an item holds more than one receipt under the same id they keep the order the record carried them in

units.days: integer day offsets from the plan start; negative days lie before the horizon
units.hours: run_hours is what one planned order occupies at its item's work centre on the day it loads; a centre's daily_hours is what it can start in a working day
units.qty: whole units; a planned order's qty is what is RELEASED and receipt_qty is what ARRIVES good
